newsitem.title: FRANCE: GOLF-CARTER BACK AFTER BRAIN OPERATION.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-CARTER BACK AFTER BRAIN OPERATION.

text.p: Britain's David Carter makes his playing comeback at Thursday's $490,000 Cannes Open, just two months after emergency brain surgery.
He collapsed after practice for the Dubai Desert Classic in February and was later found by friends at his hotel barely conscious.
Scans revealed fluid on his brain and he was operated on to relieve pressure.

It could well be a victorious return to Royal Mougins for Carter. He broke the course record last year, shooting a nine-under-par second round 62 before finishing two strokes behind winner Raymond Russell.
Scot Russell is looking to kick-start his season after the European Tour's two-week break for the U.S. Masters.
Russell has made a moderate start, a ninth place in the recent Portuguese Open his best finish as he lies 69th in the European 1997 rankings.

None of the Europeans who featured at Augusta play in the south of France, but several Ryder Cup aspirants in Mougins have been affected by the finishes in the U.S. Masters and will seek to renew their places in the cup table.
Thomas Bjorn, the Dane who edged out Russell and Ireland's Padraig Harrington for the 1996 Rookie of the Year award, also returns after recovering from injury during the Desert Classic.
Bjorn was relegated to fourth in the Ryder Cup rankings by virtue of Costantino Rocca's winnings as top European in the Masters, and he is anxious to reclaim third place.
One of the favourites for the Cannes title will be Frenchman Jean Van de Velde, who was knocked from eighth to ninth.
Elventh-placed Briton Peter Mitchell, the last winner before the break, targets the 10th place he moved to by winning in Madeira.
Australia's Desert Classic winner Richard Green makes his first appearance since Dubai.
